description: A hearty Kenyan stew of tender goat meat simmered with onions, tomatoes and spices until rich and flavourful.

steps.instruction: Brown the goat meat in hot oil for 8–10 minutes in a heavy pot.
Add chopped onions, garlic and ginger and cook until softened and golden.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a thick sauce.
Add water and salt, cover and simmer on low heat for 1 to 1.5 hours until the meat is very tender and the sauce has thickened.
Serve hot with ugali, rice or chapati.

description: Fragrant Kenyan pilau rice cooked with tender goat meat, pilau masala and caramelised onions.

steps.instruction: Fry onions in oil until deep golden brown, about 15 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger and pilau masala, stir for 2 minutes. Add goat meat and brown.
Add 2 cups water, cover and simmer until meat is tender, about 40 minutes.
Add washed rice and remaining water, season with salt. Cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes until rice absorbs water.
Let steam for 5 minutes, fluff and serve with kachumbari.

serving_suggestion: Serve with kachumbari and a cold drink.

description: Goat meat marinated with garlic and lemon, grilled over charcoal until charred and juicy—a Kenyan favourite.

steps.instruction: Mix lemon juice, crushed garlic, oil, salt and pepper. Rub over goat meat and marinate for 20 minutes.
Grill over medium charcoal or barbecue for 30–40 minutes, turning occasionally, until charred and cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into pieces and serve with kachumbari.

description: Beef liver pan-fried with onions, tomatoes and a touch of garlic—a quick, nutritious Kenyan dish.

steps.instruction: Slice liver into thin strips and rinse. Pat dry.
Heat oil and sauté onion until softened. Add garlic if using and cook for 1 minute.
Add liver and cook on high heat for 3–4 minutes until browned.
Add chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook for 5–7 minutes until tomatoes break down and liver is cooked through. Serve hot.

description: Tender beef liver simmered with plenty of onions in a rich tomato sauce, a comforting Kenyan stew.

steps.instruction: Slice liver into strips. Heat oil and sauté onions until deep golden and sweet.
Add liver and brown for 3–4 minutes. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add salt and water, simmer for 10–15 minutes until liver is tender and sauce thickens. Serve.

description: Beef liver stir-fried with chilli, onions and tomatoes for a spicy Kenyan twist.

steps.instruction: Slice liver thinly and chop chilli. Heat oil and sauté onion and chilli until fragrant.
Add liver and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until browned.
Add tomatoes and salt, cook for 5–7 minutes until tomatoes soften and liver is cooked. Serve hot.

description: Dried dagaa simmered in a tangy tomato and onion sauce, a nutritious lakeside staple.

steps.instruction: Rinse dagaa and drain. Heat oil and fry dagaa for 3–4 minutes until slightly crisp. Remove.
In the same oil, sauté onion until golden. Add tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Return dagaa to pan, add water and salt. Simmer for 8–10 minutes. Serve hot with ugali.

description: Dried dagaa simmered in a creamy coconut and tomato sauce, a coastal Kenyan variation.

steps.instruction: Rinse dagaa. Sauté onion until soft, add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add dagaa and coconut milk.
Simmer for 10–12 minutes until thick. Season and serve with rice or ugali.

description: Dried dagaa cooked with collard greens, onions and tomatoes, a nutritious Kenyan meal.

steps.instruction: Rinse dagaa. Sauté onion until golden, add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add dagaa and cook for 3 minutes.
Add sliced collard greens and salt, stir-fry for 5–7 minutes until greens are tender. Serve with ugali.

description: Firm Nile perch steaks simmered in a rich tomato and onion gravy—a hearty fish stew from Lake Victoria.

steps.instruction: Season Nile perch with salt. Heat oil and fry fish for 3–4 minutes per side until golden. Remove.
Sauté onions and garlic until soft. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add water, return fish and simmer for 10 minutes until heated through. Serve with ugali or rice.

description: Nile perch fillets fried until golden and crispy, a simple Kenyan fish dish.

steps.instruction: Cut Nile perch into fillets or chunks. Rub with salt and lemon juice.
Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Fry fish for 4–5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Drain and serve.

description: Nile perch simmered in a creamy coconut curry with tomatoes, onions and mild spices.

steps.instruction: Season fish with salt. Sauté onion until soft, add curry powder and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Pour in coconut milk and simmer gently.
Add fish and cook for 10–12 minutes until cooked through and sauce thickens. Serve with rice.

serving_suggestion: Serve with coconut rice or chapati.

description: Smoked fish simmered in a rich tomato and onion sauce, a specialty of Kenya's lakeside communities.

steps.instruction: Soak smoked fish in warm water for 10 minutes to remove excess salt. Drain and cut into pieces.
Heat oil and sauté onions until soft. Add garlic if using and cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they form a sauce.
Add fish and water. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until fish is heated through and sauce is flavorful. Serve hot.

description: Smoked fish gently simmered in a creamy coconut and tomato sauce—a rich, smoky stew from Kenya's lakeside communities.

steps.instruction: Soak smoked fish in warm water for 10 minutes. Drain and flake.
Heat oil and sauté onions until soft. Add tomatoes and cook until they form a sauce.
Pour in coconut milk and water. Add fish and simmer for 10–15 minutes until stew thickens. Season and serve.

description: Smoked fish simmered with beans in a tomato-onion sauce, a protein-rich Kenyan stew.

steps.instruction: Soak smoked fish for 10 minutes, clean and flake. Sauté onion until golden.
Add tomatoes and cook until saucy. Add beans and fish.
Add water and salt, simmer for 10 minutes. Serve hot with ugali.

description: Tender tilapia fillets simmered in a spiced coconut sauce—a coastal Kenyan classic often served with rice.

steps.instruction: Season tilapia fillets with salt. Heat oil and lightly fry fillets for 2 minutes per side. Remove.
Sauté onions, garlic and ginger until fragrant. Add tomatoes and curry powder and cook until saucy.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer. Return fish to pan and cook for 10–12 minutes until cooked through and sauce thickens.
Serve hot with rice or ugali.

serving_suggestion: Serve with coconut rice or chapati.

description: Tilapia fillets marinated with lemon and garlic, grilled until flaky and golden.

steps.instruction: Mix lemon juice, crushed garlic, oil, salt and pepper. Coat fillets and marinate for 10 minutes.
Heat a grill pan or barbecue. Grill fillets for 4–5 minutes per side until cooked through and golden.
Serve hot with kachumbari or salad.

description: Tilapia fillets simmered in a tangy tamarind and tomato sauce, a coastal Kenyan speciality.

steps.instruction: Soak tamarind in hot water and extract juice. Fry tilapia fillets in oil until golden, remove.
Sauté onion until soft, add tomatoes and cook until saucy. Add tamarind juice and water.
Return fish to pan and simmer for 10 minutes. Season and serve with rice.

description: Pigeon peas stewed with onions, tomatoes and spices, a coastal Kenyan favourite.

steps.instruction: Boil pigeon peas in water for 30–40 minutes until tender. Drain, reserving liquid.
Sauté onion and garlic in oil until soft. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add cooked pigeon peas and a little reserved liquid. Simmer for 10–15 minutes. Season and serve with rice.

description: Tender pigeon peas simmered in creamy coconut milk with onions and mild spices—a coastal Kenyan staple.

steps.instruction: Boil pigeon peas in water until tender, about 30 minutes. Drain.
Sauté onion and garlic until soft. Stir in curry powder.
Add cooked pigeon peas and coconut milk. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until thick. Season and serve with rice.

description: A hearty one-pot Kenyan dish of maize and pigeon peas cooked with onions.

steps.instruction: Soak maize and pigeon peas overnight. Boil in water for 45–50 minutes until tender.
Sauté onions in oil until golden. Add cooked maize and peas.
Season with salt and simmer for 10 minutes. Serve hot with greens.

name_en: Kenyan Lentil and Minced Beef Stew
name_sw: Mchuzi wa Dengu na Nyama ya Kuchonga
description: A hearty Kenyan stew combining lentils and minced beef with onions and tomatoes—protein-rich and flavourful.

steps.instruction: Sauté onions and garlic in oil until soft. Add curry powder and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add lentils-or-minced-beef blend and stir to coat.
Add water and salt, simmer for 25 minutes until lentils and meat are tender and stew thickens. Serve with rice.

description: A hearty, protein-rich Kenyan soup made with lentils, onions, tomatoes and garlic.

steps.instruction: Sauté onions and garlic in oil until soft. Add tomatoes and cook until softened.
Add lentils and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 25–30 minutes until lentils are soft.
Season with salt and serve hot with bread or chapati.

description: A one-pot Kenyan pilau rice cooked with minced beef, lentils, onions and spices.

steps.instruction: Fry onions until golden. Add lentils-or-minced-beef and brown.
Add pilau masala and rice, stir to coat. Add water and salt.
Cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes until rice and lentils are cooked. Fluff and serve.

description: A traditional Kalenjin fermented milk, slightly sour and smooth, served as a nutritious drink or accompaniment to ugali.

steps.instruction: Bring fresh milk to a boil, then cool to lukewarm.
Stir in sour milk as a starter culture (and salt if using).
Pour into a clean jar and leave in a warm place for 1–2 days to ferment until thick and sour. Stir and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve alongside ugali or as a refreshing drink.

description: A warm Kalenjin porridge of millet flour stirred with sour milk, eaten for breakfast or as a nourishing drink.

steps.instruction: Mix millet flour with 1 cup water to form a smooth paste.
Bring remaining water to a boil, stir in paste and cook for 8–10 minutes until thickened.
Remove from heat and stir in sour milk (and salt if using). Serve warm.

description: Stiff ugali served with traditional sour milk, a Kalenjin-inspired Kenyan combination.

steps.instruction: Boil water and salt, gradually add maize flour and stir until firm. Shape ugali.
Serve the hot ugali with chilled or room-temperature sour milk alongside.
Eat by dipping pieces of ugali into the sour milk.

description: Ripe bananas dipped in a light batter and fried until golden—a sweet Kenyan snack.

steps.instruction: Mix flour, sugar and water into a smooth batter.
Peel bananas and cut into chunks. Dip into batter.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown, about 2–3 minutes. Drain and serve warm.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a snack with tea.

description: Sweet bananas simmered in coconut milk with a touch of sugar and cardamom.

steps.instruction: Peel and slice bananas.
Combine coconut milk, sugar and cardamom in a pot and bring to a simmer.
Add bananas and cook for 10 minutes until soft and syrupy. Serve warm.

description: A creamy Kenyan smoothie made with ripe bananas, milk and a touch of sugar.

steps.instruction: Peel and chop bananas.
Blend bananas, milk and sugar until smooth.
Pour into glasses and serve chilled.

description: Chicken pieces simmered in a savory tomato and onion base—a comforting everyday Kenyan meal.

steps.instruction: Boil chicken pieces with salt and water until tender, about 25–30 minutes. Reserve broth.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and cook 1 minute. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add boiled chicken and reserved broth. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until flavors meld. Serve hot with ugali or rice.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and sukuma wiki.

description: A fragrant Kenyan spiced rice dish cooked with pilau masala, beef and caramelised onions—a festive staple.

steps.instruction: Heat oil and fry onions until deep golden brown, about 15 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger and pilau masala, stir for 2 minutes. Add beef and brown.
Add 2 cups water, cover and simmer until beef is tender, about 30 minutes.
Add washed rice and remaining water, season with salt. Cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes until rice absorbs water.
Let steam for 5 minutes, fluff and serve with kachumbari.

serving_suggestion: Serve with kachumbari and a cold drink.

description: A colourful Kenyan curry of potatoes, carrots and green beans in a spiced tomato sauce.

steps.instruction: Chop potatoes, carrots and green beans. Sauté onion until golden. Add curry powder and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add potatoes and carrots, stir and cook for 5 minutes. Add green beans, salt and water.
Cover and simmer for 15–20 minutes until vegetables are tender. Serve with rice or chapati.

description: Fragrant rice cooked in coconut milk—a coastal Kenyan favourite often served with fish or stew.

steps.instruction: Rinse rice. Heat oil and sauté onion until soft.
Add rice and stir. Pour in coconut milk, water and salt.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid absorbed. Fluff and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with fish curry or bean stew.

description: Tender beans simmered in a rich tomato and onion sauce, a protein-packed Kenyan staple.

steps.instruction: Soak beans overnight or boil for 5 minutes and let sit for 1 hour. Drain and boil in fresh water for 45–60 minutes until tender.
Sauté onions in oil until golden. Add garlic and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add cooked beans and a little reserved liquid. Simmer for 10–15 minutes. Season and serve with ugali.

description: Soft, layered flatbreads made from wheat flour, a beloved accompaniment to stews and tea.

steps.instruction: Mix flour and salt. Add water gradually and knead into a soft dough.
Divide into balls, cover and rest for 30 minutes. Roll thin, brush with oil, fold into spiral and roll again.
Cook on a hot pan for 2–3 minutes per side, brushing with oil, until golden.

serving_suggestion: Serve with beef stew or beans.

description: A stiff maize flour porridge that is the staple food of Kenya, served with vegetables, meat or fish.

steps.instruction: Bring water and salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Gradually add maize flour while stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat and keep stirring for 8–10 minutes until firm and pulls away from pot. Shape and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with sukuma wiki, beans or meat.

description: Sautéed collard greens cooked with tomatoes and onions—Kenya's most popular everyday vegetable side dish.

steps.instruction: Wash collard greens, remove stems and slice thinly.
Heat oil and sauté onions until soft. Add garlic and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add greens and salt, cook for 5–7 minutes until wilted but still bright. Serve with ugali.

description: A fresh, zesty salad of tomatoes, red onions and lemon juice—the classic Kenyan condiment.

steps.instruction: Chop tomatoes and red onion. Finely chop coriander.
Combine in a bowl, squeeze lemon juice over and sprinkle with salt.
Toss gently and serve fresh with grilled meats or rice.

serving_suggestion: Serve with nyama choma or pilau.

description: Tilapia simmered in a spiced tomato and curry sauce—a flavorful Kenyan fish dish.

steps.instruction: Clean and score tilapia. Fry in oil for 3–4 minutes per side until golden. Remove.
Sauté onion until soft. Add tomatoes and curry powder, cook until thick sauce.
Add water, return fish and simmer for 8–10 minutes. Serve with rice or ugali.

description: A rich, nutty stew made with groundnuts, tomatoes and onions—often served with rice or ugali.

steps.instruction: Roast groundnuts lightly, then grind into a paste.
Sauté onions until golden. Add tomatoes and cook until soft. Add groundnut paste and water, stir well.
Simmer for 15–20 minutes until thickened. Season and serve with rice or ugali.

description: Soft, sweet fried dough triangles—a beloved Kenyan teatime snack.

steps.instruction: Mix flour, sugar and salt. Add milk and knead into a soft dough. Rest for 15 minutes.
Roll out and cut into triangles.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown. Drain and serve warm.

description: A one-pot Kenyan dish of rice cooked with beans and a tomato-onion base—hearty and economical.

steps.instruction: Sauté onion until golden. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add beans, rice, salt and water.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender. Fluff and serve.

description: Small dried sardines cooked in a rich onion and tomato sauce—a classic dish from Lake Victoria.

steps.instruction: Rinse omena well and drain. Dry-fry for 2 minutes to remove moisture.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add omena and salt, stir and simmer for 5–7 minutes. Serve with ugali.

description: A creamy, spiced pumpkin soup with coconut milk and a warm hint of cinnamon and cumin.

steps.instruction: Sauté onion and garlic until soft. Add diced pumpkin, cumin and cinnamon, stir.
Add water and simmer for 20–25 minutes until pumpkin is tender.
Blend until smooth. Stir in coconut milk and salt, simmer 5 minutes and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with crusty bread or as a starter.
